title: Walsingham letter-book, Feb 1572/3: Burghley to Walsingham, port name read as St Valery, BL Harley MS 260 f. 419 (DECODE R8364)

steps.what: Downloaded the two R8364 images with the DECODE cookie (decrypt-custom filesrv).
Identified f. 419 as Walsingham's letter-book; the cipher letter as Burghley to Walsingham, Feb 1572/3.
Found the letter printed in Digges 1655 p. 327, cipher undeciphered.
Transcribed the cipher tokens from the scans (26 tokens).
Place-name cribs for the 7-sign run, pooled with the R8361 run's shared signs; no unique alphabet.
CSP Foreign x, Feb 1573 (BHO pp. 243-271): letter not calendared, no decipherment.
Reopened: Digges p. 245 (Walsingham to Smith, Sept 1572) prints ~90 cipher signs, so the letter-book's cipher corpus is far larger than the earlier 25-sign count.
Located every cipher passage in Digges 1655 by hOCR word confidence and two page-by-page subagent scans of all 457 images; ~45 passages cropped and listed (digges_corpus.tsv).
CSP Foreign ix-x searched for letters 'partly in cipher, deciphered' to pair with Digges; no. 527 (10 Aug 1572) is deciphered but Digges omits its cipher sentence.
Tu 2012 thesis gives the key's shelfmark, TNA SP 106/2 f. 141A (Walsingham cipher 1571), and Cotton Vespasian F VI originals; neither online (DECODE lacks f. 141A; Vespasian F VI not digitised).
Viewed DECODE SP 106/2 keys R341-R354; R343 (f. 50, Norris-period, with Deepe/Calles/Dover) and R341 do not give sense or VALERY.

Aligned the port group across five copies in four letters (Digges pp. 301, 303, 313, 327; Harley R8363, R8364): six signs, constant 1st and 3rd; with the Vespasian F VI catalogue entry for a ship kept waiting at St Valery (Dec 1572), read VALERY.
Retried the nine-sign run with the partial alphabet (H = E) and cribs (passport, safe conduct, the Queene, Lord Seton, the Regent).

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The six-sign place name was read as (St) Valery by aligning five copies of the same homophonic group in four letters (Digges 1655 and Harley 260) with the BL catalogue entry for Cotton Vespasian F VI item 111, a French letter asking for a ship to wait at St Valery.
outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher_tokens.txt, cipher tokens: the 6-sign port read of 26 tokens
outcome.notes: Port read as (St) Valery, grade M. Nine-sign run, name codes 3, II, tt and the cover-name markers unread; key SP 106/2 f. 141A and the Cotton Vespasian F VI original not reachable. Verified by the same word in five copies across four letters and by the St Valery ship in the Vespasian F VI catalogue.

gaps.item: nine-sign run '^ 4 d H m 11 11 I J'
gaps.detail: key SP 106/2 f. 141A not online; original in Cotton Vespasian F VI not digitised; one known letter
single occurrences, no key or gloss

gaps.item: [9] markers x5 and 3 after names x3
gaps.detail: cover-name markers; the names they stand for were not copied

prior.where: Digges 1655 p. 327 prints the letter with the cipher undeciphered; no decipherment found in print or on DECODE

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
